findings.title: [P0] Parse `cached.value`, not the `{ value, stale }` wrapper
findings.body: `Cache.get` now returns `Promise<{ value: string; stale: boolean } | null>` (src/cache.ts:5-6), but the caller still calls `JSON.parse(cached)` on that result. `JSON.parse` requires a `string`, so this fails TypeScript compilation (`Argument of type '{ value: string; stale: boolean; }' is not assignable to 'string'`); if executed, every non-null cache hit coerces the wrapper to `"[object Object]"` and throws a `SyntaxError`. Trigger: any cache hit on `loadProfile` — no special input needed. The fix is `JSON.parse(cached.value)`.

findings.title: [P2] Handle stale cache entries instead of always serving them
findings.body: The new cache contract deliberately surfaces `stale`, but `loadProfile` only distinguishes `null` from non-`null` and never reads the flag (repo-wide search confirms no other consumer). If `readWithMetadata` returns expired entries flagged `stale: true` — the reason the field exists — those profiles are served indefinitely with no refresh path, since `api.loadProfile(id)` runs only on a `null` miss. If serve-stale is the intended strategy, that deserves an explicit comment; otherwise a stale hit should trigger revalidation.

findings.title: [P3] Add tests for the new cache-result contract in loadProfile
findings.body: The repository contains no test files at all, so nothing exercises the new metadata-bearing return shape or the cache-hit/miss branches of `loadProfile`. That gap is exactly what let the type-incompatible `JSON.parse(cached)` change land unnoticed. Adding even a minimal unit test for the hit/miss/stale paths would catch regressions in this contract.
